geometry_edits.rationale: Preserve the protected hall but use its section family to soften the stacked profile into a more coherent occupied roof/section.
A shed/folded-like section is more compatible with an active neighborhood mass than a purely tiered stepped profile.
Keep the long-axis section logic aligned with the visible dominant stretch of the mass.

graph_edits.rationale: Turn the primary mass from a generic court container into a clearer carved public void that can answer the access edge.
Increase the scale of the subtraction so the void reads as a usable public court rather than a shallow notch.
Align the court opening with the programmed access side so the ground response becomes legible at the street edge.
Retarget the terrace link to the access side to strengthen the public threshold and avoid a semantically opposite ground response.
Reduce the bend severity so the upper mass reads as a calmer continuous continuation over the carved ground rather than a tiered object.
Simplify the executable path to improve form continuity and reduce the appearance of stacked fragments.

rationale: The candidate is visually coherent across the four views and the parcel containment looks acceptable, but the dominant idea reads as a compact stepped block rather than a clearly programed neighborhood-living mass with an active public threshold. The blue access edge is not convincingly answered by a legible entry seam, court, undercut, or public ground figure; the mass feels semantically closed on the access side. The stepped silhouette is coherent enough to avoid being rejected as random, but it leans toward arbitrary tiering rather than a capacity-bearing section with public consequence. Reference language supports a court/void-and-bridge strategy, yet the current form does not fully exploit that logic. Overall it is repairable, but not program-fit as shown.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Cultural/community-center language is close, but the candidate lacks the same legible courtyard-public edge relation and feels more like stacked tiers than a single void-driven figure.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Large carved central void with a clear bridge/threshold condition and calm enclosing masses.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Office/campus scale is somewhat larger and more porous than the candidate; useful for void hierarchy, not for copying the exact fragmentation.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Interlocking masses around a central court with terraces and undercut ground response.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Much smaller and more horizontal; the candidate should borrow the active threshold logic, not the one-story typology.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Simple active-ground pavilion with a clear public edge, canopy-like threshold, and compact massing.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Counterfactual only: this is too strongly residential-ribbon in character and pushes the candidate toward an unrelated stepped-housing typology.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced/sectional massing can support inhabited roof landscapes and continuous circulation.

warnings: Access edge response is weak relative to the verified road frontage.
The form trends toward a stacked/stepped object instead of a clearly active neighborhood threshold.
Voids are present only faintly; they do not yet read as usable public space.
Avoid over-learning the counterfactual 8 House terrace ribbon; this program wants a grounded mixed-use court/terrace, not a residential megastructure.
